venue: Quantum (the open journal for quantum science; quantum-journal.org)
scope_fit: Broad quantum science, theory and experiment; acceptance judged on correctness, significance and clarity. Editorial policy says correct work that incrementally improves a limited technique is below threshold and asks for a very significant technical or conceptual contribution. No explicit statement on negative results was found. Precedent (already in repo bibliography): Chakrabarti et al., 'A threshold for quantum advantage in derivative pricing', Quantum 5, 463 (2021) and Stamatopoulos et al., Quantum 4, 291 (2020), so finance resource-threshold work is demonstrably in scope; the question is significance, not topic.
format_and_source: Submission is by arXiv reference (quant-ph listing or cross-list required). quantumarticle.cls is encouraged but not mandatory (GitHub/CTAN). Main results and assumptions should be clear in the first couple of pages.
length_limits: No explicit length limit found on the author instructions page.
abstract_rules: No word limit stated. Optional non-technical summary for publicity. Keywords not required (not mentioned).
required_statements: Author contribution statement is mandatory (any level of detail). AI/LLM use must be disclosed inside that statement. Competing interests and funding statements not mentioned on the author page (acknowledge funding conventionally).
ai_policy: Author instructions: if an LLM or other AI model was used in producing the work, the scope of that use must be disclosed in the author contribution statement; listed examples include grammar-checking, reformatting, text production, image production, bibliographic research, code or calculations. No prohibition on AI-assisted drafting found. arXiv (required host) additionally requires reporting significant use of text-to-text generative AI, says AI tools must not be listed as authors, and that each author takes full responsibility for all content regardless of how generated.
data_code_policy: Authors should publish data and code under FOSS licences whenever possible; raw data, plotted data and analysis code encouraged for research papers (encouraged, not mandated). Fits the planned frozen benchmark + D_max calculator release.
preprint_and_arxiv: arXiv posting in quant-ph (primary or cross-list) is a NECESSARY condition for consideration. Final accepted version must be uploaded to arXiv under CC BY 4.0 (same licence as publication; irrevocable). arXiv endorsement policy updated 21 Jan 2026: automatic endorsement now needs BOTH an institutional email AND prior authorship of an accepted paper in the same endorsement domain; otherwise a personal endorsement from an established author in that domain is required; arXiv staff cannot endorse. A first-time quant-ph submitter from VIT Vellore therefore likely needs a personal endorser. A q-fin primary with quant-ph cross-list would need endorsement for q-fin (and cross-list rules) - verify in the arXiv submission UI.
fees_and_waivers: Voluntary APC: EUR 600 standard (from Jan 2025), EUR 100 discount option, or full waiver; payment page says no justification is needed for a waiver, only notify the journal. No country-based rule needed. Effectively zero-cost for an unfunded author in India.
review_model_and_time: Single-blind peer review overseen by an editor; referees get about 1 month. Stated indicative timeline: >=2 weeks to assign editor, 2-3 weeks to first editorial decision (desk reject / revise / referee), 2-4 months to collect reports, 1-2 months after resubmission, publication within about a week of acceptance.
risks: High significance bar (desk-reject risk if seen as a limited-technique negative case study; must lead with the general frontier/calculator and checklist). Mandatory public arXiv posting under CC BY 4.0 before review; endorsement may block a first-time submitter. Overlap with Chakrabarti et al. threshold paper must be clearly delimited (L1 checkpoint).

scope_fit: Quantum information science and technology across physics, CS, maths, engineering. Selection requires exceptional achievement in at least one of: advancing the field in new directions, linking areas/disciplines, enabling new capabilities, or addressing high-impact topics. A negative requirements frontier is topically in scope but must clear a PRX-level significance bar; no explicit statement on negative results. An editorial 'Clarifying PRX Quantum's Acceptance Criteria' (PRX Quantum 6, 020001, 2 May 2025) exists but its text could not be read here.
format_and_source: Any format for initial evaluation; single PDF sufficient for review; REVTeX preferred (Word template also offered); LaTeX source requested after acceptance. Submission via arXiv ID supported.
length_limits: Research Articles: no length limit. Perspectives 7,500 words; Tutorials 37,500 words; Comments 3,500 words.
abstract_rules: No abstract word limit found on the PRX Quantum or APS length-guide pages (APS style guidance elsewhere suggests <500 words; not verified on a primary page here). Mandatory popular summary <=250 words for non-specialists before publication. PhySH subject headings are used in APS submission (not verified as mandatory on the pages read).
required_statements: Data Availability Statement mandatory for submissions on/after 11 Dec 2024. Author contributions statement listed. Substantive AI use must be disclosed. Conflicts of interest must be reported to editors and a COI statement in the paper is encouraged.
ai_policy: APS policy updated 17 June 2026: substantive AI use (literature synthesis, data analysis, scientific reasoning, drafting or revising scientific claims, figure and code generation, translation) is permitted with disclosure; light editing/polishing need not be disclosed. Disclosure must give tool name and version, how it assisted, how it was directed and how output was verified. Location: methods section for research uses, figure captions for figures, acknowledgment statement for other uses. AI cannot be an author; authors fully accountable; authors must keep a record of AI use.
data_code_policy: Mandatory Data Availability Statement; data sharing strongly encouraged; manuscripts must contain details needed to reproduce the work; code may go in supplemental material but code release is not mandated.
preprint_and_arxiv: arXiv posting before or during review is permitted and submission via arXiv ID is supported; arXiv is NOT required.
fees_and_waivers: Gold OA, CC BY 4.0, mandatory APC USD 3,590 (2026) on acceptance. APS automatic waivers use a Research4Life-based list of ~115+ lower-income countries; India is NOT on the list, so no automatic waiver for a VIT Vellore corresponding author. Check VIT/Indian consortium agreements before submitting.
review_model_and_time: Single-anonymized peer review. 2025 journal metric: about 211 days submission to publication on average.
risks: Very high selectivity; a finance-specific negative result from one toolchain is likely to be desk-rejected unless framed as a field-level contribution. USD 3,590 APC with no India waiver. Model-version disclosure required (runtime does not expose exact model IDs per AI_USE_LOG.md; author must record what is known).

scope_fit: Full spectrum of physics plus interdisciplinary areas; papers must add to knowledge in a field 'with a connection to physics', be significant and a substantive addition. Fault-tolerant resource/requirements analysis of a quantum algorithm is plausibly in scope under quantum information; the finance application needs the physics/QIS framing (hardware clock, T-depth, logical-qubit frontier). No explicit statement on negative results.
format_and_source: Single PDF sufficient for review; REVTeX preferred; LaTeX source after acceptance; submission via arXiv ID supported.
length_limits: No length limit found for regular articles on the pages read.
abstract_rules: No abstract limit found on the pages read; APS general style guidance (not verified on a primary page here) is <500 words. Keywords via APS PhySH (not verified as mandatory).
required_statements: Data Availability Statement mandatory (from 11 Dec 2024); COI to editors and encouraged in paper; substantive AI-use disclosure; author contributions per APS style.
ai_policy: Same APS-wide policy (updated 17 June 2026): substantive AI use in drafting, reasoning, figures, code and analysis permitted with disclosure of tool name/version, role, direction and verification; disclose in methods (research uses), figure captions (figures) or acknowledgments (other uses); light polishing exempt; AI cannot be an author.
data_code_policy: Mandatory Data Availability Statement; data sharing strongly encouraged; reproducibility detail required; code release encouraged via supplemental material, not mandated.
preprint_and_arxiv: arXiv preprints permitted before/during review; not required.
fees_and_waivers: Fully gold OA (CC BY 4.0): mandatory APC USD 2,910 (2026). Automatic APS waiver list is Research4Life-based and does NOT include India. No subscription route.
review_model_and_time: Single-anonymized peer review. 2025 metrics: desk decision ~4 days, first decision after review ~56 days, submission to acceptance ~126 days, to publication ~165 days.
risks: USD 2,910 unavoidable APC for an India-based unfunded author is the main blocker. Finance readership is small; physics connection must be explicit.

scope_fit: Applied physics; listed topics include 'Quantum information science and technology'. Criteria: fresh insight into applications-based physical phenomena, significant and substantive. Computational finance is not listed; a quantum-finance requirements frontier is a weaker thematic fit (the 'applied' angle would be fault-tolerant hardware requirements: logical clock, T-throughput, width). No statement on negative results or benchmarking.
format_and_source: PDF sufficient for review; REVTeX preferred (Word template available); LaTeX source encouraged.
length_limits: Regular Articles: no length limit. Letters 4,500 words; Reviews 30,000 words.
abstract_rules: No abstract limit found on the pages read. Optional non-technical summary for promotion.
required_statements: Data Availability Statement mandatory for all published articles; substantive AI use must be disclosed in the paper; author contributions per style guide; COI to editors.
ai_policy: APS-wide policy (17 June 2026): AI-assisted drafting and other substantive uses permitted with disclosure (tool/version, role, direction, verification) in methods, figure captions or acknowledgments; light editing exempt; AI not an author.
data_code_policy: Mandatory Data Availability Statement; data sharing strongly encouraged; code not mandated.
fees_and_waivers: Hybrid: subscription route has no mandatory charge per the author page; optional OA APC USD 2,910 (2026). India not on APS automatic waiver list (irrelevant if the subscription route is used).
review_model_and_time: Single-anonymized. 2025 metrics: first editorial decision ~7 days, first decision after review ~56 days, submission to acceptance ~146 days, to publication ~177 days.
risks: Scope drift: editors may view a finance-benchmark negative result as outside 'applications-based physical phenomena' and desk-reject. Cheap via subscription route.

scope_fit: Fully OA, multidisciplinary journal for 'the finest research' on quantum information including quantum computing. Topic fits (fault-tolerant algorithm requirements), but the selectivity language and Nature branding imply a high significance bar; no statement on negative results found. Detailed aims/scope page not read.
format_and_source: Any format at initial submission (compiled PDF); LaTeX files accepted at acceptance stage; Nature reference style; formatting only enforced at acceptance.
length_limits: No explicit word limit found for Articles on the guidelines page (concision recommended).
abstract_rules: No abstract word limit stated on the guidelines page read. Keywords not mentioned.
required_statements: Data availability statement required; code availability statement required for custom code central to the claims; competing interests statement required for all accepted papers; author contributions required; LLM use documented in Methods.
ai_policy: Journal guidelines: LLMs such as ChatGPT do not satisfy authorship criteria; LLM use must be properly documented in the Methods section. Nature Portfolio AI page (traffic-light scheme, undated): language polishing is green (low risk); extensive copy editing or writing support and suggesting methods are amber (human oversight plus disclosure); presenting AI-generated hypotheses, analyses or conclusions as human-derived and assigning accountability to AI are red (not permitted); photorealistic generated images not permitted.
data_code_policy: Nature Portfolio data/code availability: data availability statement mandatory; code availability statement mandatory where custom code is central (code may be requested for peer review).
preprint_and_arxiv: Unrefereed preprints do not compromise novelty (arXiv allowed, not required).
fees_and_waivers: Mandatory gold-OA APC for Original Research: GBP 3,090 / USD 4,390 / EUR 3,690 (page did not state which currency applies to India). Automatic waivers only for corresponding authors in the world's lowest-income countries (India is not low-income); discretionary waivers/discounts for financial need must be requested AT SUBMISSION, not later. Check VIT/Indian Springer Nature OA agreements.
review_model_and_time: Not verified on primary pages read (editorial-process page not fetched); unknown.
risks: Highest APC among candidates (USD 4,390) with only discretionary waiver; high selectivity. 'Presenting AI-generated analyses/conclusions as human-derived' is prohibited, so the AI_USE_LOG must be precise and the author must personally verify claims.

scope_fit: Emerging quantum science and technology including quantum computation, simulation, engineering and ML applications; finance not named. Highly selective: work should be essential reading for a sub-field, of interest to the broader QST community, with lasting impact; Papers must be a significant advance. A requirements frontier for fault-tolerant QAE is in topical scope; the bar is significance. No statement on negative results.
format_and_source: Single PDF at submission (anonymised if double-anonymous chosen); IOP LaTeX and Word templates available; Vancouver or Harvard references; persistent identifiers (DOI/arXiv) preferred.
length_limits: No numeric word/page limit stated for Papers or Letters on the pages read.
abstract_rules: Abstract max 300 words, self-contained, no undefined abbreviations. Keywords requested for discoverability.
required_statements: Competing interests must be disclosed at submission. CRediT contributions optional (otherwise all co-authors share full responsibility). ORCID recommended. Data availability statement: IOP research-data-availability policy requires a DAS, but which IOP data policy QST follows was not confirmed on the pages read. GenAI disclosure in Acknowledgements.
ai_policy: IOP GenAI policy: permitted uses include research assistance, editing human text, generating text (authors must critically revise AI text for accuracy and plagiarism), figures from existing data, explanatory images, literature-review support. PROHIBITED: fabricating or manipulating data/results, generating or modifying reference lists, uploading reviewer reports to GenAI, generating responses to reviewers, hidden prompts. Disclose in the Acknowledgements with tool name and version and the use (template sentence provided); add methods detail if AI was part of the research process. Routine spelling/grammar editing exempt. Record-keeping of drafts and prompts encouraged.
data_code_policy: IOP data availability policy requires a data availability statement (applicability to QST not explicitly confirmed); code sharing not mandated; if code is on GitHub, deposit a DOI-issuing copy (e.g., Zenodo) and cite software with persistent identifiers.
preprint_and_arxiv: Preprints may be posted before submission provided authors keep copyright and grant no exclusive licence (arXiv default licence acceptable). arXiv not required.
fees_and_waivers: Subscription route free of charge (no APC). Optional gold OA APC GBP 2,930 / EUR 3,335 / USD 4,090. The free route removes the fee issue for an unfunded author in India.
review_model_and_time: Single-anonymous or double-anonymous at author's choice. No numeric time-to-decision stated (claims rapid decisions).
risks: Highly selective; small acceptance rate. IOP forbids using GenAI to generate or modify the reference list and to draft responses to reviewers: the BibTeX must be compiled/verified by the author and responses written by humans, which conflicts with the current agent-driven workflow unless changed. DAS applicability to be confirmed at submission.

scope_fit: Engineering applications of quantum phenomena, including quantum computation, information, software and hardware; regular, review and tutorial articles. A compiled-oracle resource analysis plus hardware-requirements frontier (T-depth, width, logical clock, T-throughput) is an engineering-requirements result and fits this scope well; finance is the application, not the subject. No statement on negative results found.
format_and_source: IEEE journal article templates (LaTeX/Word) via IEEE Author Center; submission via ieee.atyponrex.com portal.
abstract_rules: Not stated on TQE pages read; IEEE journals conventionally use a single-paragraph abstract and 'Index Terms' keywords (not verified on a TQE primary page).
required_statements: AI-generated content disclosure in Acknowledgments (IEEE-wide). Other statements (data availability, COI, contributions) not specified on the TQE pages read - check the IEEE Author Center checklist at submission.
ai_policy: IEEE journal policy: use of AI-generated content (text, figures, images, code) must be disclosed in the Acknowledgments section; the AI system must be identified, and the specific sections containing AI-generated content identified with a brief explanation of the level of AI use. AI for editing and grammar enhancement is generally outside the policy; disclosure not required but recommended. No prohibition on AI-assisted drafting found.
data_code_policy: Not specified on the pages read; IEEE supports code/data via IEEE DataPort/Code Ocean (not verified here). Unknown whether a DAS is mandatory.
preprint_and_arxiv: Preprints allowed; IEEE requires the notice 'This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication' on the first screen of posted preprints, and after acceptance the posted version must be replaced by the full IEEE citation or the accepted manuscript with IEEE copyright notice and citation. arXiv not required.
fees_and_waivers: Gold OA, CC BY or CC BY-NC-ND. APC USD 1,995 (effective 1 Jan 2024); IEEE member -5%, society member -20%; 100% waiver for low-income and 50% discount for lower-middle-income countries (World Bank). India is lower-middle income (World Bank FY26; not among the FY27 movers announced July 2026), so expected APC about USD 998 before any member discount. Confirm eligibility at submission.
review_model_and_time: Single-anonymous peer review with at least two independent reviewers (per journal listing; peer-review model not restated on the pages fetched). Timing not stated.
risks: About USD 1,000 cost even after 50% discount unless VIT pays. Lower visibility among finance readers. IEEE requires identifying which sections contain AI-generated content, so AI_USE_LOG must be section-granular.

scope_fit: Per the official About page (seen only as a search-indexed snippet; dl.acm.org blocked direct fetch): theory and practice of quantum computing, including quantum algorithms and complexity, architecture, principles and methods of fault-tolerant quantum computation, design automation, programming languages/systems, and applications. A compiled reversible-oracle resource study with a fault-tolerant requirements frontier fits 'fault-tolerant methods' and 'design automation'; negative/requirements results not explicitly addressed.
format_and_source: ACM authoring template (acmart) required for submission and publication; submission via Manuscript Central (per search snippet of author guidelines). Over-length or mis-formatted manuscripts can be desk-rejected.
length_limits: A page limit exists per the author guidelines snippet but its value could not be read (page blocked). Unknown.
abstract_rules: Unknown (author-guidelines page blocked). ACM template requires CCS concepts and keywords (general acmart convention; not verified on the TQC page).
required_statements: ORCID required for ACM authors (ACM authorship policy). Other statements unknown for TQC; AI use in the research itself must be described in the methods section.
ai_policy: ACM Policy on Authorship, updated 14 May 2026: AI used to CONDUCT research (design, data, coding, simulations, analysis, validation, artifacts such as code/datasets/figures relevant to conclusions) must be described in detail in the methods section. AI used to ASSIST WITH WRITING no longer requires disclosure. All named authors are accountable for any problematic content regardless of source; ACM may reject or retract for AI-related integrity problems. (Older ACM FAQ wording about Acknowledgements disclosure is superseded by this update.)
data_code_policy: Not verified for TQC (page blocked). ACM has an Artifacts and Reproducibility programme (badging) but whether TQC mandates data/code availability is unknown.
preprint_and_arxiv: Not verified on a TQC page (blocked). ACM generally permits arXiv preprints, but confirm in author guidelines. arXiv not required.
fees_and_waivers: From 1 Jan 2026 all ACM publications are fully OA: ACM Open institutional coverage, or APC, or waiver. ACM Journals 2026 temporary subsidy: USD 950 (with an ACM/SIG member co-author; list 1,300) or USD 1,450 (no member; list 1,800). India is listed as a World Bank lower-middle-income country eligible for a 50% geographic discount, applied automatically to the subsidised rate: about USD 475 (member) or USD 725 (non-member) in 2026. Rates for 2027 acceptances not stated. Financial-hardship waivers also exist. Check whether VIT participates in ACM Open (then APC = 0).
review_model_and_time: Unknown (not verified). Revisions expected within 30 days (minor) / 90 days (major) per search snippet of author guidelines.
risks: Venue-specific pages (scope, page limit, review model) could not be opened directly; recheck by browser before deciding. Subsidised 2026 APC may not apply if acceptance slips into 2027. CS/quantum-systems readership, little finance audience.

venue: The Journal of Computational Finance (Risk.net / Infopro Digital)
scope_fit: Numerical and computational methods for financial mathematics: finite differences/elements/spectral methods, advances in Monte Carlo and quasi-Monte Carlo, market-factor simulation, optimisation for hedging, numerical analysis, free-boundary problems. Quantum computing is not mentioned on the journal page. The classical half of the paper (RQMC/smoothing failure for discretely monitored knock-outs, T_C(eps) tables, benchmark) fits squarely; the quantum frontier would be framed as the application motivating a computational-cost benchmark. This matches the plan's pre-committed fallback contribution (benchmark/computational-finance venue). Initial editorial screen is for originality, validity and importance; out-of-scope papers may be declined before review.
format_and_source: Anonymised PDF at submission (no names or affiliations); separate title page with names, affiliations, running head <=50 characters and word count; LaTeX or Word source on acceptance; figures/tables in PDF and as separate editable files; Chicago style punctuation.
length_limits: Research papers up to 10,000 words; forum papers up to 7,000 words; stated as not strict, final decision by publisher.
abstract_rules: 150-200 words, single paragraph, standalone without references. 4-6 specific keywords required.
required_statements: Conflict-of-interest declaration mandatory (either declare or use the given no-conflict sentence). AI-use acknowledgement with each tool and its use specified. Data/code, contributions, funding statements not specified.
ai_policy: Risk Journals guidelines: uses of AI in drafting submitted papers must be acknowledged, specifying each AI tool and its use. Listed acceptable uses are limited to extracting/organising data, background research akin to a search engine, and editing aid akin to Grammarly. Generating substantive text is not among the listed uses and is not explicitly permitted or forbidden, so AI-assisted drafting of the manuscript is at best ambiguous; ask the editor before submission.
data_code_policy: No data or code policy stated on the guidelines page.
preprint_and_arxiv: Guidelines say published papers must not be posted online; pre-submission preprints (arXiv/SSRN) are not addressed. arXiv not required. Posting the accepted/published version to arXiv appears disallowed; confirm with the publisher before any arXiv posting.
fees_and_waivers: No page charges or APC mentioned for the standard (subscription) route. Open access available by arrangement (contact given on the guidelines page); OA price not stated.
review_model_and_time: Editorial screen then external, independent single-blinded peer review (the page also asks for an anonymised PDF). No timeline stated.
risks: AI policy lists only narrow acceptable uses, which may conflict with an AI-assisted drafting workflow; needs editor confirmation or human rewrite. 'Must not be posted online' restricts arXiv/open benchmark release of the article text (code/data release is separate). 10,000-word soft limit forces a compact paper. Low impact factor (~0.5) and small quantum readership; finance referees may view the quantum side as peripheral.

scope_fit: Interdisciplinary quantitative finance, theoretical and empirical, for a broad researcher/practitioner readership; listed applications include derivatives pricing and hedging and financial engineering. Quantum computing is not named. A strong-classical-comparator benchmark for option pricing (RQMC failure for discrete knock-outs, T_C(eps), D_max calculator) fits 'derivatives pricing' if written for finance readers; the quantum requirements frontier must be made accessible. Negative results not addressed. Research Letters (<=12 pages) section also exists for influential short results.
format_and_source: Word or LaTeX (journal LaTeX template available); upload PDF plus zipped LaTeX source; figures separate; original articles only; order: title page, abstract, keywords, main text, acknowledgments, declaration of interest, references, appendices.
length_limits: Typical paper no more than 35 pages including references and footnotes; word count must be included. Research Letters max 12 pages.
abstract_rules: Unstructured abstract of 200 words; 4-6 keywords; optional graphical/video abstract.
required_statements: Funding details (or state none); disclosure (competing interests) statement; declaration of generative AI use (required even if none used); data availability statement where a dataset is associated; CRediT roles supported and requested at submission; ORCID encouraged.
ai_policy: Journal requires a 'Declaration of generative AI use' statement disclosing whether and how GenAI was used in the research and manuscript preparation (state explicitly if not used). T&F AI policy: permitted uses include idea generation/exploration, copyediting/language improvement/translation, literature classification and coding assistance; disclosure must give full tool name with version, how and why it was used; AI cannot be an author; not permitted: GenAI creation or manipulation of research results/outputs, text or code generation without rigorous revision, synthetic data to substitute missing data without robust methodology. AI-assisted drafting is acceptable only with rigorous human revision and disclosure.
data_code_policy: T&F Basic Data Sharing Policy: sharing encouraged, DOI repository deposit encouraged, DAS encouraged; asked at submission whether a dataset exists. Open Science Badges supported (Open Data / Open Materials / Preregistered) - relevant because this project has a prospective specification (preregistration-like) and frozen benchmark.
preprint_and_arxiv: Preprints permitted (instructions note anonymity cannot be guaranteed if an earlier version is on a preprint server; T&F preprint policy page referenced). arXiv not required.
fees_and_waivers: NON-REFUNDABLE SUBMISSION FEE: USD 162 / GBP 121 / EUR 137 / AUD 216, payable by card at submission (Research Letters exempt for an initial period). No APC for the subscription route; optional Open Select OA APC (amount via APC finder, not read). No India-specific waiver of the submission fee found.
review_model_and_time: Editor screening then single-blind review by two anonymous referees. Metrics: 15 days to first decision, 98 days to first post-review decision, 45 days acceptance to online; 23% acceptance rate; aim to give first decision within six months.
risks: USD 162 non-refundable submission fee (author must pay personally; this agent cannot). Finance referees may see the quantum half as out of their expertise; framing must lead with the classical benchmark and decision rule. 35-page typical limit is compatible.

scope_fit: Theoretical financial mathematics plus computational articles that introduce new methods and algorithms representing significant (explicitly 'as opposed to incremental') improvements on modern numerical implementations. A negative requirements frontier is not a new classical method; it would only fit if the measured RQMC/smoothing failure for discretely monitored knock-outs or the budget identity is presented as a rigorous mathematical/computational contribution. Weak fit for the paper as framed.
format_and_source: SIAM LaTeX macros (siamart) are the SIAM norm; the SIFIN instructions page (epubs.siam.org) was behind a bot-verification wall and was NOT read. Short communications section exists.
abstract_rules: Unknown (instructions page not readable); SIAM journals conventionally require keywords and MSC codes (not verified).
required_statements: AI use must be reported in Acknowledgements or Declarations with a statement that the authors assume responsibility for all content (from search snippet of the SIAM AI policy v2.0, May 2026; the policy page itself was not readable). Others unknown.
ai_policy: SIAM News article by the SIAM VP for Publications (1 May 2026, read in full): authors must be human; AI tools may be used provided usage is disclosed per the SIAM Publications AI Policy; examples of accepted uses include finding literature, developing proofs and algorithms, coding, running experiments and getting feedback on drafts; editors may reject for poor scholarship even without a technical error; fabricated references lead to a minimum one-year submission ban; repeated substandard AI-aided submissions can also lead to a ban. SIAM referees are currently prohibited from using AI tools. Per search snippet of epubs.siam.org/artificial-intelligence (Version 2.0, effective May 2026; not opened): disclose in Acknowledgements or Declarations with a responsibility statement.
preprint_and_arxiv: Per search snippet of SIAM author information: posting on a preprint server or as a technical report is not prohibited. arXiv not required. Not verified on an opened page.
fees_and_waivers: Subscription journal: no mandatory APC found. Optional open access on acceptance for a one-time fee of USD 3,750 (search snippet of epubs.siam.org/journal-authors; not opened). No India-specific waiver information found.
risks: Explicit 'significant, not incremental' new-method criterion makes a requirements/negative paper a poor fit. Strict penalties (one-year ban) for fabricated references: every citation must be human-verified. Key venue pages blocked by bot verification; recheck manually if considered.

scope_fit: Theoretical and experimental quantum technology including 'quantum information, communication and computation'; excludes foundations and non-technical applications such as 'quantum economics'. Technical quantum-algorithm finance work is demonstrably in scope (already in repo bibliography: Manzano et al., 'Alternative pipeline for option pricing using quantum computers', EPJ QT 12:28 (2025); Miyamoto IQAE bias, EPJ QT 11:42 (2024)). Review criteria are scientific robustness, originality and clarity (no stated 'significance' bar), which suits a careful negative/requirements result.
format_and_source: Word, RTF or TeX/LaTeX; Springer Nature LaTeX template encouraged; editable source required in production; double spacing, line and page numbers. Figure titles max 15 words, legends max 300 words.
length_limits: No word limit found on the research-article guidelines page read.
abstract_rules: Abstract summarises aim and findings, minimal abbreviations, no citations (no word limit found on the page). 3-10 keywords.
required_statements: Mandatory 'Declarations' section with: Availability of data and materials; Competing interests; Funding; Authors' contributions; Acknowledgements (write 'Not applicable' where relevant). LLM use documented in Methods.
ai_policy: Journal guidelines: LLMs do not satisfy authorship criteria; use of an LLM should be properly documented in the Methods section (or a suitable alternative part if no Methods). Springer journal-policies AI risk framework: green (permitted) = language polishing, structure/formatting suggestions, data cleaning; amber (permitted with human oversight, verification and disclosure) = drafting explanatory summaries, comparing results to literature, extensive copy editing or writing support, suggesting methods; red (not permitted) = presenting AI-generated hypotheses/analyses/conclusions as human-derived, fabricating data/citations/results, undisclosed LLM core research reasoning, assigning authorship to AI.
data_code_policy: Availability of data and materials statement mandatory for all manuscripts; for some data types repository deposit is mandatory (per guidelines); Springer data policies apply. Code availability is conventionally covered in the same section.
preprint_and_arxiv: Springer Nature encourages preprints on any server at any time during review; not prior publication. arXiv not required.
fees_and_waivers: Fully OA (CC BY or CC BY-NC-ND): APC GBP 1,790 / USD 2,190 / EUR 1,990 plus VAT/local taxes, price set at acceptance date. Automatic waivers only for corresponding authors in the world's lowest-income countries (India is lower-middle income, not eligible automatically). Discretionary waivers/discounts for financial need must be requested AT SUBMISSION. Check VIT / Indian Springer Nature OA agreements via the institution selector.
review_model_and_time: Single-anonymous; typically two or more reviewers; criteria robustness, originality, clarity. Timing not stated on pages read.
risks: About USD 2,190 APC unless a discretionary waiver is requested at submission or VIT has a Springer agreement. Lower prestige than Quantum/QST. Red-category rule on AI-generated conclusions requires the author to own and verify every claim.

scope_fit: All areas of quantum information science. Regular Articles are 'high quality articles of arbitrary length on any aspect of QIS' (Letters must show significant innovation). No significance-for-the-broad-field bar for Regular Articles, so a rigorous negative/requirements study of fault-tolerant amplitude estimation for pricing is in scope. Precedent in repo bibliography: Tanaka et al., ML amplitude estimation, QIP 20, 293 (2021). Already the recommended first target in docs/JOURNAL_REENGINEERING_RESEARCH_2026-09-09.md.
format_and_source: Single document with title page (single-blind); .docx or LaTeX (Springer Nature LaTeX template); Author Contribution and Competing Interest information must be entered in the submission interface (only that text is published).
length_limits: Regular Articles of arbitrary length (no limit).
abstract_rules: The guidelines page is internally inconsistent: one section says an abstract of 80-100 words, another says 150-250 words; no undefined abbreviations or unspecified references. 4-6 keywords. Author should confirm with the editorial office or satisfy both by staying at about 100-150 words only after checking.
required_statements: Data Availability Statement mandatory for original research (Springer Nature research data policy); author contributions and competing interests via submission interface; LLM use documented in Methods.
ai_policy: LLMs do not satisfy authorship criteria; LLM use should be documented in the Methods section (or a suitable alternative part). 'AI assisted copy editing' (improving human-generated text for readability, style, grammar, spelling, tone) need not be declared, but this exemption excludes generative editorial work and autonomous content creation; human accountability required. Springer AI risk framework: extensive writing support is amber (permitted with oversight and disclosure); presenting AI-generated analyses/conclusions as human-derived or fabricated citations are red (not permitted).
data_code_policy: Springer Nature research data policy: sharing strongly encouraged; Data Availability Statement mandatory for all original research.
preprint_and_arxiv: Springer Nature journal policies encourage preprints on any server at any time during review; not prior publication. arXiv not required.
fees_and_waivers: Hybrid: subscription route has no APC. Optional OA APC GBP 2,190 / USD 3,090 / EUR 2,490 plus taxes. Zero cost for an unfunded author in India via the subscription route.
review_model_and_time: Single-blind peer review. Timing not stated on the pages read.
risks: Lower visibility/prestige than Quantum or QST; subscription route limits open readership (mitigate with an arXiv preprint and a Zenodo archive of the benchmark). Abstract-length inconsistency on the official page must be resolved.
